method: six independent reviewers over the landed Phase 9 diff, then three independent refuters per finding with distinct lenses (is it true / is it reachable / is it already handled), defaulting to refuted when uncertain
dimensions: Evidence integrity and the audit record
Lifecycle, idempotency and recovery (Phase 6 guarantees under Phase 9's collection-keyed outbox)
SECURITY BOUNDARY: the PowerShell batch and the transport (engine/powershell/service/{operations,executor,schemas,main}.py, engine/collectors/{powershell_client,graph_client}.py)
Collector behaviour equivalence (4 Graph collectors restructured to bounded concurrency, 2 PowerShell collectors restructured to batch)
The API contract and the frontend (backend-api/app/api/v1/scans.py, schemas/provenance.py, main.py; frontend api/client.ts, hooks/usePoll.ts, Scans/ScanDetailPage.tsx, Scans/ScansPage.tsx)
Gates, claims and what the tests actually prove (Phase 9 — performance and maintainability)
note: The review ran while fixes from an earlier Gemini pass were still landing, so many findings were fixed BEFORE their refuters read the file. A 'refuted' verdict here therefore means 'the refuter could not find the defect in the code as it stood', which for most of these is because it had just been fixed -- not that the finding was wrong. Every finding is listed with what was actually done.

survived_all_three_refuters.title: A per-member failure the code itself marks retryable is written straight to a terminal error row; the identical failure in a single-control group is retried

The /execute-batch client timeout (120 s) is shorter than the service's own batch budget (300 s), so long batches always fail client-side while the pwsh child keeps burning one of four execution slots
A completed scan can be stranded on screen as permanently "running" with stale counts if the single full read at the terminal transition fails
POWERSHELL_MAX_BATCH is a dead setting: the documented bound on how many operations share one remote session is never read

refuted_or_already_fixed.title: A transient OPA subprocess failure is classified as deterministic, terminal-erroring a whole collection group on the first attempt with zero retries
refuted_or_already_fixed.location: engine/worker/tasks.py:123 (_is_retryable) and engine/worker/tasks.py:876 (runtime_version call site); engine/opa_client.py:96

A Graph 401 is never retried even though the pooled client now caches one token for a whole collection group
The `claimed` guard does not prevent double collection: `evaluate_collection` re-derives its members from the database, so a control served by a legacy per-result row is collected twice, concurrently
The non-ready fallback still fails the whole scan: an unpublishable per-result row ratchets to `dispatch_retry_exhausted` and errors every control in the scan
refuted_or_already_fixed.location: engine/worker/execution_plan.py:96-104 and engine/worker/dispatcher.py:98-114 (`_recreate_pending_children` unplannable branch), with engine/worker/tasks.py:628

refuted_or_already_fixed.title: Drift has no recovery: a worker death between the finalising commit and `_drift_after_finalisation` loses the comparison permanently, and the reconciler's own finalising path never calls drift
`run_scan`'s `pragma: no cover - rejected above already` is wrong: a non-string `data_collector_id` reaches the per-result fallback
The batch transport gives up at 120s while the service is allowed 300s, so a successful long batch is reported as a collection failure
build_batch_script's ConvertTo-Json depth is off by one: the wrapper costs two levels, not one, so batched evidence is truncated one level earlier than the same operation run singly
verify_sharepoint_tenant leaks a pooled Graph client on every SharePoint collection group
Four concurrent pwsh children, each now living up to 300s, in a 512MB / 1 CPU container
Batched PowerShell collapses N x 120s of per-operation budget into a single 120s client timeout, and the 300s server budget is unreachable
build_batch_script under-compensates ConvertTo-Json depth by one level, so batched evidence truncates earlier than the serial path did
cloud_only_admins / admin_license_footprint: the two-pass split changes which exception surfaces, turning a retryable transport failure into a non-retryable one
mailboxes: per-mailbox alignment now depends on UPN uniqueness rather than position, and zip can silently shorten the enrichment
A single failed terminal read strands the scan detail page on "Running" forever, because the ETag is committed before the work it gates
usePoll forks a second poll chain whenever the tab becomes visible while a request is in flight - overlapping ticks and a permanently doubled request rate

refuted_or_already_fixed.title: GET /scans/{id} now validates every result row three times per request and materialises the policy_source text it is about to discard
PERF-03 "bounded per-item collector concurrency" is not verified by any test: all four collectors can be reverted to a strictly serial loop and the entire engine suite stays green
PERF-02 pooled Graph transport: the one assertion that names pooling is dead code, and removing pooling entirely leaves all 30 transport tests green
tools/perf/scan_load_report.py: two of the seven rows it prints as Phase 9 savings are measurement-order artifacts whose sign flips when the two topologies are swapped
The load report's per_control column does not model the pre-Phase-9 engine, so the PowerShell-session delta it prints understates and mislabels the batching saving
Result pagination is an unreachable feature chain: the backend parameters have no test, and the typed client wrapper has no call site
The frontend conditional-GET client is the only untested link in the "conditional summary polling" chain, and every test that exercises the poll mocks it away
Two pre-existing "stops polling" tests were left watching getScan after Phase 9 moved the poll target to getScanSummary, so they no longer detect continued polling

The summary ETag is built from a hand-maintained field list that already omits a field the summary publishes (dispatch_count), and the test that claims to cover this is a six-case hardcoded parametrize
Phase 5's "every client execution path validates before I/O" gate was not widened to the three new PowerShell batch entry points, and the batched Docker path has no test at all
Vacuous, proxy and self-describing assertions in the new Phase 9 tests
A pre-existing integration assertion was loosened from equality to set membership, so it now passes under either dispatch shape
